question: During which week of intrauterine life does the development of the human heart typically begin?
explanation: Cardiogenesis begins early in the third week of intrauterine life because the growing embryo urgently needs a functional circulatory system. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: What critical embryonic process positions the future chambers of the heart into their correct anatomical orientation?
explanation: Cardiac looping folds the straight primitive heart tube into an S-shape, placing the future chambers in their proper anatomical positions. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following heart wall layers is primarily responsible for the pumping action of the heart?
explanation: The myocardium is the thick, middle muscular layer of the heart wall that contracts to pump blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle significantly thicker than that of the right ventricle?

options.A: It receives deoxygenated blood directly from the lungs.
options.B: It pumps blood against a much lower resistance pulmonary circuit.
options.C: It must generate higher pressure to circulate blood throughout the entire body.
options.D: It contains more valves than the right ventricle.

explanation: The left ventricle needs a thicker wall because it pumps blood through the systemic circulation, which requires much higher pressure than the pulmonary circuit. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which part of the heart is directly responsible for powering pulmonary circulation?
explanation: The right side of the heart receives deoxygenated blood and pumps it to the lungs for pulmonary circulation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What hormone is released by specialized atrial myocardial cells when stretched by high blood volume to help reduce blood pressure?
explanation: Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) is secreted by stretched atrial cells to promote sodium and water excretion, lowering blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What physiological event produces the first heart sound (S1, or 'lub')?

options.D: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves

explanation: The first heart sound is caused by the sudden closure of the atrioventricular valves at the beginning of ventricular systole. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: During which phase of the cardiac cycle do the ventricles contract while all four heart valves remain closed, causing a rapid rise in pressure?
explanation: Isovolumetric contraction occurs when the ventricles contract with closed valves, increasing pressure without altering blood volume. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which structure is recognized as the natural pacemaker of the heart because it generates electrical impulses at the highest rate?
explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node sets the baseline heart rate by initiating electrical impulses faster than any other part of the conducting system. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary physiological purpose of the delay that occurs at the Atrioventricular (AV) node?

options.A: To speed up the heart rate during exercise
options.B: To allow the atria enough time to empty blood into the ventricles
options.C: To prevent electrical impulses from traveling backward into the atria
options.D: To initiate the second heart sound

explanation: The AV node delay ensures that the atria finish contracting and completely empty their blood into the ventricles before ventricular systole starts. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which component of an ECG tracing corresponds to ventricular depolarization?
explanation: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization, the electrical event that precedes ventricular contraction. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h6)

question: What clinical condition is commonly indicated by an elevation or depression of the ST segment on an ECG?
explanation: Alterations in the ST segment are classic diagnostic markers for inadequate blood supply to the heart muscle, such as ischemia or acute myocardial infarction. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h6)
